slot.brief: Rank a set of cyclic/acyclic species (including an antiaromatic ion and an aromatic ion) by stability using Hückel's rule.

stem: Select the decreasing order of stability of the following anions, considering resonance and cyclic conjugation.
options: Cyclopentadienyl anion ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^-$) > allyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_5^-$) > propyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7^-$) > cyclopropenyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_3^-$)

Cyclopropenyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_3^-$) > cyclopentadienyl anion ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^-$) > allyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_5^-$) > propyl anion ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_7^-$)

verdicts.working: Cyclopentadienyl anion is aromatic with 6 π electrons; allyl anion is resonance-stabilized; propyl anion is localized. The cyclopropenyl anion has 4 π electrons in cyclic conjugation and is antiaromatic, making it least stable. Thus the order is Cp > allyl > propyl > cyclopropenyl.

working:
Cyclopentadienyl anion: $6\pi$ electrons, aromatic. Allyl anion: resonance-delocalized; propyl anion: localized. Cyclopropenyl anion: $4\pi$ electrons in a cyclic conjugated system, antiaromatic. Hence the order is cyclopentadienyl $>$ allyl $>$ propyl $>$ cyclopropenyl.

solution: Cyclopentadienyl anion has $6\pi$ electrons and is aromatic; the allyl anion is resonance-stabilized, whereas the propyl anion is localized. The cyclopropenyl anion has $4\pi$ electrons in a cyclic conjugated system and is antiaromatic, so it is least stable. Hence the decreasing order is cyclopentadienyl $>$ allyl $>$ propyl $>$ cyclopropenyl.
